title: Underwriting Acceptance Bulletin — Travel Protection Plans
content:
A Travel Protection Plans plan may only be quoted where the declared trip cost is at or below the plan's ceiling, where the oldest insured traveller falls within the plan's age range, and where the journey is no longer than the plan's maximum length.

A multi-trip plan is quoted on its flat annual premium rather than on the trip cost, and covers its stated number of journeys in the policy year, each no longer than the plan's maximum length.

A quotation stands for the working day it was produced and is re-rated afterwards, because the rating depends on the distance to departure.

The pre-existing medical condition waiver is granted only on a plan that offers it and only where the policy is bought within the plan's waiver window counted from the first payment toward the trip. A waiver claimed outside that window is refused at issue rather than argued at claim.

Children under the plan's free age travelling with an insured adult are covered at no additional premium and are still counted as insured travellers for every per-traveller limit.

A traveller already on a journey may not buy cover for it; cover is never issued with retrospective effect.

## Points of acceptance

The three acceptance tests are cumulative: the declared trip cost, the age of the oldest insured traveller and the length of the journey must each fall within what the plan carries. A risk that passes two and fails the third is not quoted on that plan.

A case that is accepted: a party of two whose oldest traveller is 58, declaring a trip cost of 9000.00 USD on a journey of 21 days, is within the ceiling, the age range and the maximum length of Trip Basics Standard, and the plan may be quoted.

A case that is not accepted: the same party declaring a trip cost of 9000.00 USD on a journey of 52 days is outside the maximum journey length of Trip Basics Standard, and the plan may not be quoted for that journey however comfortably the cost and the age sit within their limits.

A waiver case: where the plan offers the pre-existing medical condition waiver and the policy is bought inside the plan's waiver window counted from the first payment toward the trip, the waiver is granted at issue. Where the purchase falls outside that window, the waiver is refused at issue, and the refusal is settled then rather than left to be argued when a claim is made.

A child under the plan's free age travelling with an insured adult adds nothing to the premium, but is counted among the insured travellers wherever a limit is stated per insured traveller.
